**One command, a safer upgrade path, and tools to see and fix what is going on.** Nivyx 2.2 is about the `nivyx` command and the release pipeline around it. **The traffic engine — nftables / WinDivert / PF interception, DNS-over-HTTPS, TLS record fragmentation, the decision ladder, fail-open — is unchanged from 2.1.**

## One public command: `nivyx`

- `dpictl` and `dpi-proxy-ctl` are gone: not shipped, not installed, not documented. `nivyx` is now the actual implementation on every platform (Windows: `nivyx.cmd` + `nivyx-impl.ps1`).
- Upgrading from 2.1 removes only Nivyx's own old command files (`/usr/local/bin/dpictl`, `/usr/local/bin/dpi-proxy-ctl`, the old wrappers in the install folder). A different tool that happens to share a name is left alone — this is tested.
- Internal names (service, launchd label, PF anchor, nftables table, config folders, the `dpi-proxy` engine binary) are unchanged on purpose so upgrades keep your config and learned state; see `docs/development.md`.

## New commands

- **`nivyx update [--check]`** — updates from the official GitHub release. Verifies the SHA-256 against the release's `SHA256SUMS` *before* installing, swaps the files, restarts the service, health-checks it, and **restores the previous version automatically if the new one fails**. Your config and learned state are never touched. Only runs when you ask; no telemetry.
- **`nivyx repair`** — the mutating twin of `doctor`: restarts or re-enables the service, removes stale status files and stale Nivyx firewall state (nftables table / PF anchor / WinDivert driver), restores permissions, drops damaged learned-decision lines, and explains every action. Touches only Nivyx-owned state.
- **`nivyx stats`** — uptime, connection counters, DNS counters and strategy-cache size, local only, no host names.
- **`nivyx diagnose DOMAIN`** — now explains the path in three layers (DNS, HTTPS, the decision: source, strategy, TTL); `--verbose` adds the detail.
- **`nivyx config show|path|check|set|unset`** — safe access to manual rules: one line changed, a `.bak` kept, nothing changed unless you ask; manual rules still always win over learning.
- **`nivyx help [command]`**, a shorter `--help`, `man nivyx` (Linux/macOS) and shell completion for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell.
- `nivyx status` stays a five-line summary.

## Privacy

- `nivyx support-bundle` now also masks host names in log lines and the status file (counts only). A regression test checks the redaction.

## Release and supply-chain hardening

- Every release file has signed build provenance (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo kadireren7/nivyx`) and an SPDX SBOM ships with the release.
- GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs; CI runs read-only and only the publish job can write. See `docs/security.md`.
- A release is only published if the **v2.1.0 → candidate upgrade test** passed on Linux, Windows and macOS (arm64 and Intel), next to the existing end-to-end tests.
- New Linux asset `nivyx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (engine + CLI) is what `nivyx update` installs; the bare `nivyx-linux-x86_64` binary is still published.

## Installers

- All three installers end with `Nivyx is running.` and the commands to try; the README has one install card per platform.

## Reliability and speed

- `nivyx status` on Linux is about 2.4× faster (one `systemctl` call instead of three, no per-field process launches): 88 ms → 37 ms on the test machine.
- New tests: stale and damaged state, rules removed externally, DoH providers unreachable, truncated/bad/unrunnable updates, and the cross-platform command parity check.

## Audited, deliberately not changed

IPv6, QUIC, the decision ladder, DNS handling and network-change behavior were audited (`docs/audit-v2.2.md`); no engine change was justified. Known limitations are documented there, notably: on Linux and Windows, LAN-only names (`printer.lan`) and captive-portal DNS are not answered by the network's own resolver (macOS does); and CI runners have no IPv6, so IPv6 is covered by unit tests and field use rather than end-to-end CI.

## Assets

`nivyx-linux-x86_64`, `nivyx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `nivyx-windows-x86_64.zip`, `nivyx-macos-arm64.zip`, `nivyx-macos-x86_64.zip`, `nivyx-2.2.0.spdx.json`, `SHA256SUMS`.
